text:
nina: thinking about how we expose runtime "knobs" for tenant-level cost/latency tradeoffs. tenant wants to opt into "aggressively cheap" routing during non-peak hours. question: should we (A) bake that into compile-time policy variants (cheap/normal/premium) or (B) let runtime multiply/shift compiled scores under tight bounds? pros/cons?

carlos: compile-time variants are straightforward for auditing and A/B, but explosion of variants is annoying. runtime knobs let us respond to live signals (queueing, node health) without re-compiling, which seems useful.

anya: operationally we care about two things: 1) observability (why did we pick a route?) and 2) safety (can't let a tenant's cheap-mode hurt other tenants). any runtime approach needs immutable compiled guardrails.

kevin: propose hybrid: compiler emits normalized base_scores + per-tenant ceiling/floor for runtime adjustments. runtime can only apply a scale in [floor, ceiling] and must attach a compiled_snapshot_id to traces. this gives live control with replayability.

nina: agree. also want to avoid per-request heavy math. runtime op should be a single scalar multiply per scorer + an early reject for hard constraints.

ops-bot: heads up: experiment "probe-driven-weighting" running in us-east-1; dashboard -> https://grafana.company/board/probe-drive

carlos: two other constraints: multi-model outputs (different scorer value ranges) and fairness across SLA tiers. we should normalize scorer outputs at compile-time (e.g., min-max or percentile clipping) so runtime scales are consistent.

anya: on fairness, compiler should enforce inter-tenant caps tied to SLA tier. e.g., a basic-tier tenant compiled ceiling cannot exceed 0.3 relative weight in overload conditions. runtime sees that ceiling but cannot override it.

kevin: for traceability include fields: compiled_snapshot=sha256(...), runtime_adjustment=0.42, adjustment_reason="offhours". Persist these on the request and in the route decision event.

nina: good. plan draft:
1) Compiler outputs: normalized scorers, hard constraints, per-tenant floor/ceiling, compiled_snapshot id.
2) Runtime surface: a tiny allowlist API: { knob_name: "defer_to_cheap", scale: 0.0-1.0, reason: string } that must fit in [floor, ceiling].
3) Sidecar shim: implement overlay in sidecar first; it intercepts chooser decisions and applies scale before final selection. helps rollback and isolates perf impact.

carlos: sidecar is nice but watch out for increased RPC hops or latencies. microbench the sidecar path vs in-process.

kevin: also add a policy-lint step: at compile-time, flag any tenant cap that violates global fairness invariants or allows starving higher SLA. treat lint failures as build breaks for policy pushes.

anya: test matrix: unit tests for numeric stability, sim with traffic mixes, canary with 1% tenants, and an emergency kill switch which drops runtime scaling to 1.0 (no change).

nina: example compiled payload (proto-like) to include in RFC:
```
compiled_snapshot: "sha256:abcd1234"
scorers: [ { name: "latency", norm_base: 0.7 }, { name: "cost", norm_base: 0.35 } ]
constraints: { hard_blacklist: ["model-x"], min_weight: 0.1 }
tenant_caps: { tenant_id: "acme", floor: 0.5, ceiling: 0.9 }
```
runtime overlay accepted by sidecar: `{"knob": "defer_to_cheap", "scale": 0.6, "reason": "offhours_bulk"}`

kevin: performance note: do a microbenchmark for 1M requests simulated with sidecar multiply; target <2% p50 latency increase. if larger, consider moving scale into chooser library with a safe guardrail.

carlos: logging/telemetry: emit a decision event with compiled_snapshot, runtime_scale, and a small histogram of score deltas so we can detect runtime biasing spikes.

anya: rollout plan: feature-flag the sidecar overlay per-region, start with canary tenants, collect fairness and unit-cost metrics for 48 hours, then expand. add an automated revert if cross-tenant fairness drops >5%.

nina: i'll draft RFC with payload examples, lint rules, and the checklist for sim + canary. siapa volunteer to run perf microbench?

kevin: i'll run microbench and the sim. carlos will own telemetry hooks.

ops-bot: created ticket infra/arch-3302224444 -> RFC draft required.

nina: thanks all, i'll post the RFC link when ready.
